v.title: Ferguson Faces 7‑Game Ban After Red Card Chaos
v.excerpt: Duncan Ferguson faces a seven‑match ban after a red card in Glens’ loss to Cliftonville, threatening the club’s survival hopes.
v.body:
## Quick take
Duncan Ferguson has been handed a seven‑match suspension after a red card in Glens’ 3‑2 loss to Cliftonville. The ban will see him miss the rest of the season’s key fixtures.

## What happened
The match ended 3‑2 for Cliftonville, with Ferguson receiving a straight red after a reckless challenge on the opposing striker. The disciplinary panel, after reviewing the footage, deemed the tackle “unnecessary and reckless,” awarding a seven‑game ban, the longest for a single offence in recent Ulster League history.

Glens, already struggling in the league, are now forced to shuffle their backline. Ferguson, who has been a talisman for the club’s defensive solidity, will be absent for the next seven games, potentially jeopardising their fight against relegation.

## Why it matters
- **Glens’ survival hopes**: Ferguson’s absence could expose a frail defence, turning Glens into a prime target for rivals. A string of losses could push them into the relegation zone, affecting the club’s financial future.
- **Player reputation**: The ban tarnishes Ferguson’s image as a disciplined leader. His reputation in the league may suffer, impacting future transfer interest or coaching prospects.
- **League integrity**: The decision underscores the league’s zero‑tolerance stance on dangerous play, sending a clear message to all players that reckless challenges will carry heavy penalties.

## What's next
Glens will have to rely on their bench depth for the upcoming fixtures. Keep an eye on the squad rotation list released next week; a younger defender might step into Ferguson’s role. Watch how the team adapts in the next match against a top‑table side—will they maintain their defensive shape or collapse without their veteran? The outcome will set the tone for Glens’ survival battle.

*Source: [Glens boss Ferguson apologises after seven-game ban](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cm0evqv7nyq5o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
